<reason>CON won a tight, high-quality clash by making the motion easier to decide: a binding common retirement clock either hits living grids or unbinds itself. PRO’s coordination-and-support case was coherent and its pressure answers were honest, but those answers (keep plants running as a surviving breach; no unfunded clock) let CON crystallize an unfunded wall versus a yielding deadline. PRO never showed why a shared political date improves buildout over domestic bankability.</reason>
<best_rebuttal>CON’s retirement-day fork after PRO’s A1/A2: treating overruns as leftover “breach” paperwork means coal is not phased out on a common schedule, while keeping the date means shortages.</best_rebuttal>
